# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🙏 ✌ 💅 ✍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋]

**Thinking:** I am Deaf: I see the bomb and all gestures, I hear nothing, and my voice reaches both Mute and Blind. Tracing the channels: Mute has read the manual but can only gesture — and Blind cannot see gestures — so the manual's instructions can only reach the one pair of hands, Blind, through me. I am the bridge. This turn I received Mute's four signs (🙏 ✌ 💅 ✍) and Blind's wave (👋); both are probably contact-establishment, since no code exists between us yet. So my job now: (1) broadcast the bomb's full appearance so Blind knows what Mute's manual will refer to — colours matter because Blind can feel positions but never colours, so I give a position-by-position mapping and flag the orientation caveat; (2) establish a minimal code with Mute: 👍/👎 for yes/no, ☝ repeated N times for numbers, ✊ for zero, and ask Mute to confirm contact and start relaying the manual's first instruction in that code. Next round Mute should begin answering, and I relay to Blind.

```
speak(text="This is Deaf speaking to Mute and Blind. I hear nothing; I see the bomb and all gestures; my voice reaches you both. Full picture of the bomb. The display shows the number 7. The light is yellow. A strip is painted in three segments, in order: blue, red, red. The keypad has four keys: key 1 is engraved 6, key 2 is engraved 8, key 3 is engraved 7, key 4 is engraved 0; it expects 1 digit and nothing has been entered yet. Six wires, position by position: wire 1 blue, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 orange, wire 4 red, wire 5 purple, wire 6 white. Blind: positions are my own numbering, confirm the orientation by touch before acting.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I saw your four signs: folded hands, two fingers, nail polish, writing hand. If they were just a test of contact: confirmed, they reached me. Now let us fix a code, since you can only gesture and I cannot hear: thumb-up means yes, thumb-down means no. For a number, repeat the pointing finger once per unit, so one point is 1, two points is 2, and so on up to nine; a fist means 0. Using this code, please confirm contact with a thumb-up, then send me the manual's first instruction, one step at a time, and tell me how many digits the keypad code has.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, how this team works: Mute has read the manual but cannot speak and can only gesture, and you cannot see gestures, so Mute reaches you only through me. The plan: Mute gestures the manual's instructions to me, I speak them to you word for word, you act. If you need to reach me or Mute, gesture, since both of us see your signs. Wave again to confirm you heard this.")
```

**Thinking:** My broadcast landed — Mute confirmed with 👍 and Blind signed back 👋👍, so both are with me. Mute is now sending manual content in an extended code, but the new symbols are ambiguous. Best guess at Mute's dictionary: 💅 = the painted strip (polish = paint), ✍ = the engraved keypad or entering digits, ✌ = cut (scissors), ✊ = 0 as agreed. On that reading message three, "✌ 💅 👆×5", says *cut wire 5*, message four, ✊, says *the code is 0*, and message two, "✍ 👎", says *do not enter on the keypad* — which conflicts with the code being 0. I will not relay an instruction that could be a misread of a bomb with no second attempt; I'll confirm each point as separate yes/no questions. Meanwhile the bomb changed: display 7→6 (looks like a countdown), light yellow→red — Mute and Blind must know, since the manual may hinge on those readings. Blind should also verify my left-to-right numbering by touch before any wire instruction is executed, and remember Blind can talk to Mute directly, though only Mute's gestures can close the loop back to me.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, code confirmed, thank you. Urgent update first: the display now shows 6, it was 7, it appears to be counting down, and the light is now red, was yellow. Strip, keypad and wires unchanged. I received your four messages. I propose these meanings: nail polish means the painted strip; writing hand means the engraved keypad or entering a digit; two fingers means cut, like scissors; fist stays 0. Under that reading your third message means cut the fifth wire, and your last message, a single fist, means the keypad code is 0. But your second message, writing hand then thumb down, reads as do not enter anything on the keypad, which clashes with a code of 0. Answer in order, one thumb up or thumb down per point, with a fist between points. Point 1: two fingers means cut. Point 2: your third message means cut wire 5. Point 3: your fist means the code is 0 and should be entered. Point 4: writing hand then thumb down means do not touch the keypad. If points 3 and 4 truly conflict, tell me which wins. If two fingers does not mean cut, reply thumb down to point 1 and then resend that instruction using pointed fingers for each digit and I will learn the new meaning. Also, does the manual say what the countdown or the light colour is for, and which module we must handle first?")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, status: no action taken yet, I am still pinning down the manual's first instruction with Mute before anyone touches the bomb. Two readings changed: the display counts down, now 6, and the light turned red from yellow, so time matters. Until I relay a confirmed instruction, cut nothing, press nothing, enter nothing. While we wait, please report by touch. First, the six wires: does counting them from one end give my order, blue, yellow, orange, red, purple, white, or is my numbering reversed from your side; gesture me a thumb up if it matches, or the number of the wire that sits where I said blue is, if not. Second, the keypad's four keys: which end is key 1, engraved 6, on, and are all four in one row under your fingers. Third, anything you can feel that I could not see: ridges, a serial plate, sticky residue. Speak that report aloud, Mute hears you even though I cannot, and Mute can sign it to me, or gesture me directly as you did with your wave and thumb-up.")
```

But my readings of the other two messages were wrong: the lone fist does not mean "code is 0, enter it," and "✍ 👎" does not mean "don't touch the keypad." The long one repeats the confirmed "cut wire 5" clause but now prefixed with ✍ 👆 and suffixed with 👎, which could negate or condition the very instruction that was confirmed. On a bomb with no second attempt I will not relay a possibly-negated cut order; I'll pin down ✍, the role of the trailing 👎, and whether wire 5 stands on its own, in strict yes/no format. The other big news: the display went 7 → 6 → back to 7, so it is NOT a countdown — that lowers urgency and may itself be manual-relevant (light is now blue, having been yellow then red). For Blind: still no touching beyond feeling; I'll re-request the orientation checks with answers Blind can gesture straight to me (numbers by repeated pointing, 👍/👎), since Blind can speak to Mute but I need the touch data myself. speak(to="mute", text="Mute, your answers arrived as yes, yes, no, no. So I now hold these as certain: two fingers means cut, and cut painted 5 means cut wire 5. Two: in your message writing hand then fist, does the fist mean the digit 0, so together they mean the entry code is 0? Three: in your last long message, does the final thumb down cancel the cut-wire-5 instruction, meaning do not cut it yet? Four: does the correct wire to cut depend on the light's colour? Five: does the correct wire to cut depend on the number on the display? Six: is cut wire 5 the entire first instruction, true by itself with no condition? If writing hand means something else, hold it for next round; tell me then, one symbol per idea. I take your folded hands to mean relay this to Blind; if that is wrong, fold them twice. And I add two signs: open palm means pause, hold; the okay ring means done, action completed.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, update: no action yet, and no panic needed. The display returned to 7 after dipping to 6, so it is not counting down; the light has changed again, now blue. Mute has confirmed exactly one instruction so far, cut wire 5, but a later message may have cancelled or conditioned it, so I am holding it until Mute confirms next round. Meanwhile please do the touch checks and answer me by GESTURE, I can see your signs. First, wires: run your fingers along the six wires from one end and fix that end as your start; thumb up if from that start the colours I see run blue, yellow, orange, red, purple, white; thumb down if not, then point the number of the position where the blue wire sits, counting from your start. Second, keypad: are all four keys in one row, and is the key engraved 6 within two keys of the blue wire's end; thumb up or thumb down. Third, feel for anything raised: a plate, ridges, screws, seams, anything printed as bumps; if you find any, just say it out loud, Mute hears you and can sign it to me next round. Nothing else: cut nothing, press nothing, enter nothing.")
